The leak check misses Windows paths because it searches the JSON text instead of the transcript's values.

**Cause:** `src/leaks.py:8` builds the search text with `json.dumps(actions).lower()`. JSON escapes every backslash as `\\`, so the transcript value `C:\Users\dana` is stored in the search text as `c:\\users\\dana`. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so `secret.lower() in text` never matches. Forward-slash paths have no characters to escape, so `/home/dana` matches as written.

**Reproduced:**
- Transcript target `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana` → `[]` (missed)
- Same transcript, secret written with doubled backslashes `C:\\Users\\dana` → found, which shows the mismatch is the escaping
- Transcript target `cat /home/dana/x`, secret `/home/dana` → found

**Why the tests don't catch it:** `tests/test_leaks.py` only covers the POSIX form `/home/dana`. No test includes a backslash path.
